slot.brief: For an implicit curve, find the equation of tangent/normal or dy/dx at a given point without solving for y.

stem: The curve $e^{x-y+1}+\ln(x^2+y^2)+xy=3+\ln 5$ passes through $(1,2)$. Its normal there is

verdicts.working: At (1,2), F_x=1+2/5+2=17/5 and F_y=-1+4/5+1=4/5. The normal has slope F_y/F_x=4/17, so its equation is 4x-17y+30=0.

working:
$p=\dfrac{dy}{dx}:\ e^{x-y+1}(1-p)+\dfrac{2(x+yp)}{x^2+y^2}+y+xp=0$. At $(1,2)$: $(1-p)+\dfrac{2(1+2p)}{5}+2+p=0\Rightarrow p=-\dfrac{17}{4}$. $m_{\text{normal}}=-\dfrac{1}{p}=\dfrac{4}{17}$. $y-2=\dfrac{4}{17}(x-1)\Rightarrow 4x-17y+30=0$.

Independent check: At (1,2), F_x=1+2/5+2=17/5 and F_y=-1+4/5+1=4/5. The normal has slope F_y/F_x=4/17, so its equation is 4x-17y+30=0.
solution:
Let $F(x,y)=e^{x-y+1}+\ln(x^2+y^2)+xy$. At $(1,2)$, $F_x=17/5$ and $F_y=4/5$, so the normal slope is $F_y/F_x=4/17$.
$$y-2=\frac{4}{17}(x-1)\quad\Rightarrow\quad 4x-17y+30=0.$$
